feed_state_name: Fresh clarified or prefiltered green juice
soluble_protein_state: mostly native soluble and membrane-associated protein
dominant_fouling_mechanism: rapid adsorption/pore blocking followed by cake/gel formation
recommended_prefiltration: strainer or 50-10-1 um bag filtration; fine bag filtration optional for 60 nm ceramic membrane
required_inputs: DM, protein, particle size, pH, viscosity or proxy
notes: Recent clover-grass work suggests soluble/colloidal foulants dominate rather than coarse particles.

soluble_protein_state: partly denatured; green proteins preferentially removed
dominant_fouling_mechanism: aggregate deposition and residual colloid fouling
required_inputs: remaining soluble protein, particle size, heat history
notes: Higher base flux is assumed after upstream solids removal; heat-created aggregates may still foul.

primary_particles: protein aggregates, co-precipitated pigments and minerals
required_inputs: precipitated protein, particle size, zeta potential, pH, cake compressibility
notes: Use membrane as solid-liquid separator and diafiltration washer; assumptions must be reported.

primary_particles: protein aggregates, LAB cells, plant colloids
dominant_fouling_mechanism: cell-protein mixed cake, pore blocking and EPS fouling
recommended_prefiltration: none if product is retentate; coarse screen for equipment protection
required_inputs: cell biomass, precipitated protein, residual sugar, lactic acid, viscosity, pH
notes: Designed to couple directly to the lactic fermentation datasets.

primary_particles: few particles; soluble proteins and low-MW compounds
notes: Recommended downstream concentration step for white-protein product.

primary_particles: microbial solids, mineral fines and colloids
required_inputs: TSS, ions, alkalinity, pH, microbial solids
notes: Outside protein-recovery calibration; reusable as a generic downstream unit with a separate component database.
